newsitem.title: BRAZIL: France calls for Euro-Latin summit.
newsitem.headline: France calls for Euro-Latin summit.

text.p: French President Jacques Chirac proposed on Wednesday that European Union and Latin American leaders meet in their first summit next year to lay the groundwork for an ambitious partnership.

Chirac, on a state visit to Brazil, told Congress Europe and Latin America, both rejecting world domination by a single power, had a major role to play in a world free of the Cold War split. "Like Europe, South America will be tomorrow one of the great poles of the world now being shaped," he said.

South Americans and Europeans, sharing common roots and the same vision of economic development, social progress and regional integration, must develop new solidarities, he said. "Let us be ambitious ... I propose that for the first time in history a summit gather ... before the end of 1998, the heads of state of Europe and Latin America."
He said the summit meeting "will have to set the foundations for a new and ambitious partnership."

Chirac said the summit should include European Union and Mercosur countries on its first day and on the second day be enlarged to include Latin American Rio Group countries. French officials said the proposed summit would be held every two years and Brazil's President Fernando Henrique Cardoso proposed that the first one be held in Rio de Janeiro.

While Chirac did not mention the United States by name, his address followed in the footsteps of his mentor Charles de Gaulle's drive to counter U.S. dominance. De Gaulle was the last French leader to tour Latin America, in 1964, before ties grew chilly as the region went through a period of dictatorship and the foreign debt crisis of the 1980s.
Chirac made clear before embarking on his week-long tour of five South American nations that he intended to challenge U.S. influence and woo Latin Americans to Europe.

He started his tour on Tuesday in Brazil, Latin America's biggest country and the most powerful economy in the Mercosur customs union, and is to visit the group's three other partners, Uruguay, Paraguay and Argentina, as well as Bolivia, which is linked to the group by a free trade agreement.

Chirac hailed Mercosur as the world's fourth most powerful economic group, outshining in some fields the emerging "dragons" of southeast Asia. "It is natural the European Union and Mercosur turn toward each other. ... Their similarities, shared history, well-understood interests, their passion for their identity and their rejection of a unipolar world demand they get closer," he said.

He called for wider cooperation with Brazil to prevent financial crises, promote development, encourage disarmament and combat drugs and international terrorism. He said Brazil's return to economic stability set the scene for a speedy development of trade and for French investment, which has started to pick up after a long period of neglect.
Travelling with four cabinet ministers and some 20 leading French businessmen, Chirac is due to visit Brazil's economic capital Sao Paulo on Thursday.

French carmaker Renault is building a $1 billion plant in Curitiba and state utility Electricite de France heads a consortium that bought up power utility Light. French group Accord is studying setting up a $250 million chain of 50 hotels in Brazil.
France and Brazil signed agreements to boost cooperation on tourism, security and space industry. The European Space Agency rocket launching base is in Kourou in French Guiana, which borders Brazil.
French consortium Promotec was shortlisted for a $400 million deal to improve radar surveillance of the Amazon region, French officials said.

Chirac got a colourful welcome on Tuesday when he arrived for talks with Cardoso in Brasilia. Breaking with tradition, the two presidents dispensed with translators and spoke to one another in French. In an even more unusual break with Brazilian tradition, Cardoso is to accompany Chirac for the rest of his tour to Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo.
